papers.title: An Accurate and Efficient Approach to Knowledge Extraction from Scientific Publications Using Structured Ontology Models, Graph Neural Networks, and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of biomedical literature makes it challenging for researchers to stay current. Integrating knowledge from various sources is crucial for studying complex biological systems. Traditional text-mining methods often have limited accuracy because they don’t capture semantic and contextual nuances. Deep-learning models can be computationally expensive and typically have low interpretability, though efforts in explainable AI aim to mitigate this. Furthermore, transformer-based models have a tendency to produce false or made-up information—a problem known as hallucination—which is especially prevalent in large language models (LLMs). This study proposes a hybrid approach combining text-mining techniques with graph neural networks (GNNs) and fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) to extend biomedical knowledge graphs and interpret predicted edges based on published literature. An LLM is used to validate predictions and provide explanations. Evaluated on a corpus of experimentally confirmed protein interactions, the approach achieved a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.772. Applied to insomnia, the approach identified 25 interactions between 32 human proteins absent in known knowledge bases, including regulatory interactions between MAOA and 5-HT2C, binding between ADAM22 and 14-3-3 proteins, which is implicated in neurological diseases, and a circadian regulatory loop involving RORB and NR1D1. The hybrid GNN-LLM method analyzes biomedical literature efficiency to uncover potential molecular interactions for complex disorders. It can accelerate therapeutic target discovery by focusing expert verification on the most relevant automatically extracted information.

papers.title: AI Agent-Driven Framework for Automated Product Knowledge Graph Construction in E-Commerce
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of e-commerce platforms generates vast amounts of unstructured product data, creating significant challenges for information retrieval, recommendation systems, and data analytics. Knowledge Graphs (KGs) offer a structured, interpretable format to organize such data, yet constructing product-specific KGs remains a complex and manual process. This paper introduces a fully automated, AI agent-driven framework for constructing product knowledge graphs directly from unstructured product descriptions. Leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs), our method operates in three stages using dedicated agents: ontology creation and expansion, ontology refinement, and knowledge graph population. This agent-based approach ensures semantic coherence, scalability, and high-quality output without relying on predefined schemas or handcrafted extraction rules. We evaluate the system on a real-world dataset of air conditioner product descriptions, demonstrating strong performance in both ontology generation and KG population. The framework achieves over 97\% property coverage and minimal redundancy, validating its effectiveness and practical applicability. Our work highlights the potential of LLMs to automate structured knowledge extraction in retail, providing a scalable path toward intelligent product data integration and utilization.

papers.title: Hierarchical Attentional Hybrid Neural Networks for Document Classification
papers.abstract: Document classification is a challenging task with important applications. The deep learning approaches to the problem have gained much attention recently. Despite the progress, the proposed models do not incorporate the knowledge of the document structure in the architecture efficiently and not take into account the contexting importance of words and sentences. In this paper, we propose a new approach based on a combination of convolutional neural networks, gated recurrent units, and attention mechanisms for document classification tasks. The main contribution of this work is the use of convolution layers to extract more meaningful, generalizable and abstract features by the hierarchical representation. The proposed method in this paper improves the results of the current attention-based approaches for document classification.

papers.title: Combining machine learning, simulations and experiments for improved glass design
papers.abstract: The design of novel glasses with tailored properties remains a grand challenge in materials science, traditionally requiring extensive trial-and-error experimentation. This talk presents a comprehensive framework that integrates machine learning, atomistic simulations, and targeted experiments to accelerate the discovery and optimization of glass compositions. We demonstrate how large-scale machine learning models trained on experimental databases can predict glass properties across nearly the entire periodic table, enabling rapid screening of promising compositions. These predictions are refined through physics-informed graph neural networks that capture atomic-scale interactions and energy conservation principles, providing deeper insights into structure-property relationships. The framework is enhanced by automated knowledge extraction from scientific literature using our materials-specific language model (MatSciBERT) and natural language processing techniques. We showcase practical applications including the development of radiation-resistant nuclear waste glasses, scratch-resistant display glasses, and specialty glasses for space applications. The talk concludes by highlighting how this integrated approach has led to the discovery of novel glass compositions with superior properties, validated through experimental synthesis and characterization. Our results demonstrate that the synergistic combination of artificial intelligence, computational modeling, and experimental validation can significantly accelerate the glass design process while reducing resource requirements and environmental impact.

papers.title: The Deep Arbitrary Polynomial Chaos Neural Network or how Deep Artificial Neural Networks could benefit from Data-Driven Homogeneous Chaos Theory
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence and Machine learning have been widely used in various fields of mathematical computing, physical modeling, computational science, communication science, and stochastic analysis. Approaches based on Deep Artificial Neural Networks (DANN) are very popular in our days. Depending on the learning task, the exact form of DANNs is determined via their multi-layer architecture, activation functions and the so-called loss function. However, for a majority of deep learning approaches based on DANNs, the kernel structure of neural signal processing remains the same, where the node response is encoded as a linear superposition of neural activity, while the non-linearity is triggered by the activation functions. In the current paper, we suggest to analyze the neural signal processing in DANNs from the point of view of homogeneous chaos theory as known from polynomial chaos expansion (PCE). From the PCE perspective, the (linear) response on each node of a DANN could be seen as a $1^{st}$ degree multi-variate polynomial of single neurons from the previous layer, i.e. linear weighted sum of monomials. From this point of view, the conventional DANN structure relies implicitly (but erroneously) on a Gaussian distribution of neural signals. Additionally, this view revels that by design DANNs do not necessarily fulfill any orthogonality or orthonormality condition for a majority of data-driven applications. Therefore, the prevailing handling of neural signals in DANNs could lead to redundant representation as any neural signal could contain some partial information from other neural signals. To tackle that challenge, we suggest to employ the data-driven generalization of PCE theory known as arbitrary polynomial chaos (aPC) to construct a corresponding multi-variate orthonormal representations on each node of a DANN to obtain Deep arbitrary polynomial chaos neural networks.

summary: The literature on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for knowledge discovery highlights advancements in integrating GNNs with Large Language Models (LLMs) for knowledge extraction and document classification, particularly in biomedical contexts. However, challenges remain in computational efficiency, interpretability, and empirical validation across diverse domains. The integration of chaos theory into deep learning also presents theoretical opportunities for novel architectures, yet lacks practical applications. Overall, significant gaps exist in empirical studies and broader applications of GNNs in scientific literature, suggesting a need for innovative methodologies that enhance model accuracy and efficiency.
scholarly_positioning: While existing research has explored the integration of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) for knowledge extraction, significant limitations persist, particularly in computational efficiency and interpretability across diverse scientific domains. Current methodologies often focus narrowly on biomedical applications, leaving a gap in empirical validation and broader applicability to other fields of scientific literature. Furthermore, the theoretical advancements in chaos theory within deep learning remain largely untested in practical scenarios, highlighting an unresolved tension between theoretical potential and empirical application. This proposed research aims to bridge these gaps by developing a robust framework that leverages GNNs for large-scale knowledge discovery, enhancing model accuracy and interpretability while addressing the challenges of unstructured data in scientific literature.
research_scope: This empirical study will investigate the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for knowledge extraction from scientific literature, specifically focusing on biomedical research articles sourced from PubMed and arXiv. The study will evaluate a novel GNN architecture integrated with Large Language Models (LLMs) over a six-month period, comparing its performance against traditional document classification methods and existing GNN-LLM integration approaches. Primary outcomes will include model accuracy measured by Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) and F1-score, while secondary outcomes will assess computational efficiency and interpretability metrics, such as SHAP values. The research aims to bridge the gap in empirical validation of GNNs across diverse scientific domains, enhancing both model performance and interpretability in knowledge discovery tasks.
concept_definition:
The following table defines key technical concepts operationally: 
1. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs): A type of neural network designed to process data represented as graphs, enabling the extraction of relationships and features from nodes and edges in scientific literature. 
2. Large Language Models (LLMs): Advanced neural networks trained on vast text corpora to understand and generate human-like text, used here for enhancing GNN capabilities in understanding unstructured data. 
3. Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC): A performance metric for binary classification that considers true and false positives and negatives, providing a balanced measure of accuracy. 
4. F1-score: A metric that combines precision and recall to evaluate the accuracy of a model, particularly useful in imbalanced datasets. 
5. SHAP values: A method for interpreting model predictions by quantifying the contribution of each feature to the final prediction, useful for understanding model behavior. 
6. Dynamic Ontology Generation: The process of creating and updating ontologies in real-time to better capture the evolving knowledge in unstructured data, enhancing GNN performance. 
7. Interpretability: The degree to which a model's predictions can be understood by humans, assessed through methods like SHAP values and attention visualization. 
8. Safety Outcomes: Metrics indicating the reliability of model responses, including unsafe response rate (frequency of harmful outputs) and refusal precision/recall (accuracy of model refusals). 
9. User Trust: The degree to which users feel confident in the model's predictions, measured through trust calibration (alignment of perceived and actual reliability) and perceived transparency (clarity of model decisions).
technical_feasibility: The study requires access to open-source models for GNNs and LLMs to facilitate experimentation and hidden state extraction. It also necessitates labeled datasets from PubMed and arXiv for training and evaluation. Given the focus on interpretability, SHAP values will require access to model internals. The research does not explicitly mention the need for human participants or ethics approval, but if user trust is to be studied, a human-subject design will be necessary. Additionally, GPU resources will be essential for training the models efficiently. There is no mention of annotation protocols, which may be needed for dataset preparation. A feasible adjustment would be to ensure access to open-source models and clarify the need for human-subject design if user trust is a focus.
gap: Current methodologies for knowledge extraction using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are often limited by their reliance on structured ontologies, which may not adequately capture the complexities of unstructured scientific literature. This research proposes a novel GNN framework that incorporates dynamic ontology generation to enhance knowledge extraction capabilities, addressing the limitations of existing approaches.
question: How does the proposed dynamic ontology generation framework integrated with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) improve knowledge extraction accuracy and interpretability from unstructured biomedical literature compared to traditional document classification methods and existing GNN-LLM integration approaches?
theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates the integration of dynamic ontology generation as an independent variable with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance knowledge extraction accuracy (dependent variable) from unstructured biomedical literature. The theoretical framework is grounded in knowledge representation theory, where dynamic ontologies serve as mediators that improve feature extraction and contextual understanding. System-level outcomes, such as computational efficiency and interpretability, are influenced by the representation features generated by the GNN architecture. User-level outcomes, including perceived transparency and satisfaction, are moderated by the clarity of model predictions facilitated by SHAP values. The causal chain suggests that improved representation through dynamic ontologies leads to enhanced model performance, which in turn fosters user trust and satisfaction. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of dynamic ontology generation in real-time and its impact on both system and user-level outcomes.
hypothesis: Integrating dynamic ontology generation with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) will significantly enhance knowledge extraction accuracy from unstructured biomedical literature, as measured by improvements in Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) and F1-score compared to traditional methods.

Causal Pathway: The integration of dynamic ontology generation (IV) enhances the performance of GNNs and LLMs (IV), leading to improved knowledge extraction accuracy (DV). Interpretability and computational efficiency (mediators) further influence user trust (moderator), which affects overall satisfaction with the model.

Likely Confounds: Variability in dataset quality, differences in model architecture complexity, and external factors affecting user trust such as prior experiences with AI models.

Claim Boundaries: The study claims that dynamic ontology generation improves knowledge extraction accuracy but does not assert causation beyond the specified constructs. It cannot conclude that the improvements are universally applicable across all scientific domains or that user trust will always correlate with model accuracy.
methodology: Implement a hybrid GNN-LLM model that incorporates dynamic ontology generation for knowledge extraction from scientific literature. The methodology will involve training the model on datasets from PubMed and arXiv, comparing its performance against traditional document classification methods and existing GNN-LLM integration approaches. Evaluation will focus on accuracy (MCC, F1-score), interpretability (SHAP values), and computational efficiency (training time).
phd_contribution_design: This research proposes a novel framework integrating dynamic ontology generation with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance knowledge extraction from unstructured biomedical literature. The mechanism-level claim is that dynamic ontologies improve feature extraction and contextual understanding, leading to higher accuracy and interpretability in knowledge discovery tasks. Existing literature fails to adequately address the complexities of unstructured data and lacks empirical validation of GNN applications across diverse scientific domains. The falsifiable claim is that the proposed model will achieve a statistically significant improvement in Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) and F1-score compared to traditional document classification methods and existing GNN-LLM approaches. The strongest baseline for comparison will be traditional document classification methods, while ablation studies will assess the impact of removing dynamic ontology generation. Evidence will be considered robust if the proposed model consistently outperforms baselines across multiple datasets. A negative or null result would suggest that dynamic ontology generation does not significantly enhance knowledge extraction capabilities, challenging the theoretical framework and indicating a need for further exploration of GNN architectures in knowledge discovery.

proposal: This PhD research proposal aims to investigate the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) integrated with Large Language Models (LLMs) for large-scale knowledge discovery in unstructured biomedical literature, specifically targeting knowledge extraction tasks from datasets sourced from PubMed and arXiv. The core concept of dynamic ontology generation is operationally defined as the real-time creation and updating of ontologies that adapt to the evolving context of scientific literature, enhancing feature extraction and contextual understanding, thereby improving model interpretability and accuracy. This research addresses significant gaps in existing methodologies, which often rely on static ontologies that fail to capture the complexities of unstructured data, leading to inefficiencies in knowledge extraction. By integrating dynamic ontology generation, this study posits that GNNs can better contextualize information, resulting in improved accuracy metrics such as Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) and F1-score. The theoretical mechanism suggests that dynamic ontologies mediate the relationship between GNN performance and knowledge extraction accuracy, with system-level outcomes influencing user trust and satisfaction. The methodology involves training a hybrid GNN-LLM model while comparing its performance against traditional document classification methods and existing GNN-LLM integration approaches, with controls including fixed datasets and standardized evaluation metrics. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy (MCC, F1-score), interpretability (SHAP values), and computational efficiency (training time). The expected contributions include theoretical advancements through the introduction of dynamic ontology generation, technical innovations via a novel GNN architecture, empirical validation of the proposed model, and practical deployment guidelines for knowledge discovery applications. Key limitations include potential issues with data quality, generalization across scientific domains, and the need for ethical considerations if user trust is to be studied, alongside a risk analysis that identifies failure modes such as overfitting and insufficient data quality, with corresponding mitigation strategies outlined.

rubric_scores.level: 12-13: strong and clear research framing with minor conceptual weaknesses
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal clearly defines the research problem of knowledge extraction from unstructured biomedical literature using GNNs and LLMs. However, the operational definition of 'dynamic ontology generation' could be more explicitly detailed to enhance clarity. Major weaknesses: The concept of dynamic ontology generation lacks depth in operationalization, making it somewhat abstract and potentially vague. Next band requirements: To achieve a higher score, the proposal should provide a more detailed operationalization of dynamic ontology generation and clarify how it specifically addresses the complexities of unstructured data.

rubric_scores.level: 12-13: mostly coherent with minor reasoning gaps
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal presents a logical flow from problem identification to methodology, but some assumptions about the effectiveness of dynamic ontology generation are not thoroughly justified. Major weaknesses: The causal claims regarding the impact of dynamic ontology generation on knowledge extraction accuracy need stronger empirical support and clearer theoretical backing. Next band requirements: Strengthening the justification for causal claims and providing empirical evidence or theoretical rationale for the proposed mechanisms would improve coherence.

rubric_scores.level: 15-17: clear novelty with meaningful research differentiation
rubric_scores.justification: The integration of dynamic ontology generation with GNNs and LLMs presents a novel approach to knowledge extraction, addressing limitations in existing methodologies. Major weaknesses: While the proposal introduces a new framework, it could further articulate how this approach distinctly advances the field beyond existing GNN-LLM integrations. Next band requirements: To move into a higher score band, the proposal should explicitly compare its contributions to existing work and highlight unique theoretical advancements.

The methodology is generally sound, with clear metrics and controls, but lacks detailed descriptions of data preparation and potential ethical considerations. Major weaknesses: The proposal does not sufficiently address the need for human-subject design if user trust is to be studied, and it lacks clarity on data annotation protocols. Next band requirements: Inclusion of detailed data preparation protocols, ethical considerations, and a clearer outline of human-subject research requirements would enhance feasibility.

rubric_scores.level: 12-13: strong literature grounding with good comparative analysis
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal engages with relevant literature and identifies gaps, but the synthesis could be deeper, particularly in contrasting methodologies. Major weaknesses: The literature review lacks a critical synthesis that compares methodologies and articulates unresolved tensions more explicitly. Next band requirements: A more thorough comparative analysis of existing methodologies and a clearer articulation of how the proposed research addresses these gaps would improve positioning.

rubric_scores.level: 7-8: approaching PhD-level with some shallow areas
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal demonstrates a good understanding of theoretical concepts but lacks depth in discussing limitations and potential failure cases. Major weaknesses: There is insufficient discussion of trade-offs, limitations, and failure cases related to the proposed methodologies. Next band requirements: A deeper exploration of theoretical implications, limitations, and a more robust discussion of potential failure cases would enhance academic depth.

The proposal is well-structured and generally clear, but some terminology could be more precise. Major weaknesses: Minor inconsistencies in terminology and clarity could detract from the overall professionalism of the presentation. Next band requirements: Improving precision in terminology and ensuring consistent academic tone throughout the proposal would elevate communication quality.

evaluation.comments: Total score: 78.0/100. Academic level: Master's-level. Major strengths: Clear identification of a relevant research problem.; Innovative integration of dynamic ontology generation with GNNs and LLMs.; Well-defined evaluation metrics and methodology. Major weaknesses: Lack of depth in operationalization of key concepts.; Insufficient justification for causal claims and theoretical mechanisms.; Limited discussion of limitations and potential failure cases. Required improvements for true PhD-level quality: Enhance operational definitions and clarity of key concepts.; Strengthen empirical support for causal claims and theoretical mechanisms.; Provide a more comprehensive literature review with critical synthesis. Final verdict: The proposal demonstrates potential but lacks the depth and rigor expected at the PhD level, requiring significant improvements in theoretical framing, methodological detail, and literature positioning.

candidates.text: There is a lack of empirical validation of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in knowledge extraction across diverse scientific domains, particularly beyond biomedical literature. Existing studies primarily focus on specific applications, leaving a gap in understanding how GNNs can be effectively utilized in broader contexts. This research will address this gap by applying GNNs to a wider range of scientific literature, enhancing model accuracy and interpretability.
candidates.reason: This candidate clearly identifies a specific gap in empirical validation across diverse domains, grounded in existing literature.

candidates.text: The integration of chaos theory into deep learning frameworks, particularly in the context of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), remains largely unexplored in practical applications. This research will investigate how chaos theory can inform the design of novel GNN architectures, potentially leading to improvements in knowledge extraction efficiency and accuracy in scientific literature.
candidates.reason: While the novelty is high, the specificity and grounding in existing literature could be improved.

candidates.text: Current methodologies for knowledge extraction using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are often limited by their reliance on structured ontologies, which may not adequately capture the complexities of unstructured scientific literature. This research proposes a novel GNN framework that incorporates dynamic ontology generation to enhance knowledge extraction capabilities, addressing the limitations of existing approaches.
candidates.reason: This candidate is highly specific, well-grounded in literature, and proposes a feasible and novel approach.

gap.selected_text: Current methodologies for knowledge extraction using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are often limited by their reliance on structured ontologies, which may not adequately capture the complexities of unstructured scientific literature. This research proposes a novel GNN framework that incorporates dynamic ontology generation to enhance knowledge extraction capabilities, addressing the limitations of existing approaches.

candidates.text: Integrating dynamic ontology generation with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) will significantly enhance knowledge extraction accuracy from unstructured biomedical literature, as measured by improvements in Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) and F1-score compared to traditional methods.
candidates.reason: This hypothesis directly addresses the identified gap in current methodologies and is clearly testable through defined metrics.

candidates.text: The application of chaos theory principles in the architecture of GNNs will lead to improved interpretability and computational efficiency in knowledge extraction tasks, as evidenced by reduced training times and enhanced SHAP value metrics.
candidates.reason: While innovative, this hypothesis is less directly aligned with the specific gap identified in knowledge extraction methodologies.

candidates.text: A hybrid approach combining GNNs with advanced document classification techniques will yield superior knowledge extraction capabilities from scientific literature, outperforming existing GNN-LLM integration methods in accuracy and interpretability.
candidates.reason: This hypothesis is clear and testable, but does not fully address the gap regarding dynamic ontology generation.

hypothesis.selected_text: Integrating dynamic ontology generation with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) will significantly enhance knowledge extraction accuracy from unstructured biomedical literature, as measured by improvements in Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) and F1-score compared to traditional methods.

candidates.text: Implement a hybrid GNN-LLM model that incorporates dynamic ontology generation for knowledge extraction from scientific literature. The methodology will involve training the model on datasets from PubMed and arXiv, comparing its performance against traditional document classification methods and existing GNN-LLM integration approaches. Evaluation will focus on accuracy (MCC, F1-score), interpretability (SHAP values), and computational efficiency (training time).
candidates.reason: Strong alignment with hypothesis and comprehensive evaluation metrics.

candidates.text: Conduct an empirical study using a simplified GNN architecture without dynamic ontology generation to assess its baseline performance in knowledge extraction. The study will utilize a fixed dataset and compare results with traditional methods, focusing on accuracy and computational efficiency. This approach will provide insights into the necessity of dynamic ontologies.
candidates.reason: Feasible but lacks alignment with the core hypothesis on dynamic ontology generation.

candidates.text: Develop a theoretical framework for integrating chaos theory into GNNs to enhance knowledge extraction capabilities. This methodology will focus on the theoretical implications and potential architectures without empirical validation, aiming to propose future experimental designs.
candidates.reason: Theoretical focus lacks empirical grounding and practical applicability.
